key_insight: ODT predicts that in turbulent concentric annular pipe flow, curvature and radius ratio strongly reshape passive heat transfer, so the inner-wall temperature field is not well captured by a simple linear near-wall model.
engineering_relevance: The results support improved Nusselt correlations for annular thermal design, especially when wall curvature and finite Reynolds number effects matter even at low Prandtl number.
method: Stochastic one-dimensional turbulence (ODT) model with a dimensionally reduced radial coordinate
Fully resolves viscous, conductive, and turbulent advective transport
Calibrated for Pr=0.71 and 0.025 and extended across radius ratio and Reynolds number ranges
evidence_signal: The abstract reports analytical boundary-layer profiles matched against numerical ODT predictions and used to build radius-ratio-dependent heat-transfer scalings.
watch_item: The proposed correlations are tied to a fixed ODT calibration and may need revalidation outside the tested Prandtl, Reynolds, and geometry ranges.
paper_title: Numerical Simulation of Turbulent Concentric Annular Pipe Flow using One-Dimensional Turbulence (ODT): Part 2: Heat Transfer
